_about: Representative values for first models. Each entry gives the value used, the usual range, the source and the conditions under which the value applies. Site data always replace these values.

_sources.FC1979: Freeze, R.A., Cherry, J.A. (1979). Groundwater. Prentice-Hall.
_sources.CH1995: Clauser, C., Huenges, E. (1995). Thermal conductivity of rocks and minerals. In: Rock Physics and Phase Relations, AGU Reference Shelf 3, 105-126.
_sources.WW2004: Waples, D.W., Waples, J.S. (2004). A review and evaluation of specific heat capacities of rocks, minerals, and subsurface fluids. Natural Resources Research 13(2), 97-122.
_sources.G2007: Gercek, H. (2007). Poisson's ratio values for rocks. International Journal of Rock Mechanics and Mining Sciences 44(1), 1-13.
_sources.R1988: Robertson, E.C. (1988). Thermal properties of rocks. U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 88-441.
_sources.SL2013: Sellin, P., Leupin, O.X. (2013). The use of clay as an engineered barrier in radioactive-waste management - a review. Clays and Clay Minerals 61(6), 477-498.
_sources.B2017: Bossart, P., et al. (2017). Mont Terri rock laboratory, 20 years of research. Swiss Journal of Geosciences 110, 3-22.
_sources.OGS: OpenGeoSys 6.5.8 benchmark inputs (Tests/Data), used here unchanged.
_sources.I2007: Incropera, F.P., DeWitt, D.P., Bergman, T.L., Lavine, A.S. (2007). Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, 6th ed. Wiley.

granite.title: granite, sparsely fractured

ranges.hydraulic_conductivity: 1e-14 to 1e-10 m/s unfractured; up to 1e-6 m/s fractured (FC1979)

granite.conditions: intact rock mass at the model scale; fractures are not represented

sandstone.title: sandstone

ranges.thermal_conductivity: 1.5 to 4.5 W/m/K, higher with more quartz (CH1995)

sandstone.conditions: saturated; bulk density and heat capacity are for the saturated rock

opalinus_clay.title: claystone (Opalinus Clay type)

ranges.thermal_conductivity: 1.2 to 2.1 W/m/K, depends on direction to bedding

opalinus_clay.conditions: isotropic approximation of an anisotropic rock; solute values in the radionuclide example follow the OGS benchmark

clay_soft.title: soft clay (unconsolidated)
clay_soft.conditions: linear elastic; no creep or plasticity

sand.title: sand
sand.conditions: saturated; dispersivity grows with the scale of the problem

bentonite_saturated.title: compacted bentonite buffer, saturated
bentonite_saturated.conditions: saturated linear poroelastic only: swelling pressure, suction and drying are NOT represented (two-phase, unsaturated and swelling models are a commercial service)

cast_iron.title: cast iron (canister insert)
cast_iron.conditions: homogenised canister; tiny permeability and porosity only keep the porous-medium equations well posed
